title: その＋名詞 — “that ～ (near you / just mentioned)”
summary: その points to a thing or person close to the listener, or to something just mentioned. It always comes right before a noun. The set is この (near me), その (near you), あの (far from both), どの (which).

patterns.gloss: that ～ near you (その本, その店)

body.p: When you point at something near the person you speak to, use その: その本はわたしのです (that book near you is mine).
その also refers to something you or the other person just talked about. ペンを買いました。そのペンは安かったです (I bought a pen. That pen was cheap).
その needs a noun after it. To use it alone, say それ (that one): それは わたしのです.

examples.ja: その 本（ほん）は わたしのです。
examples.romaji: Sono hon wa watashi no desu.

examples.ja: そのペンを取（と）ってください。
その店（みせ）は安（やす）いです。

pitfalls: Do not say そのはなんですか. Use それ when there is no noun.
For things far from both people, use あの, not その.
